about: XML through Clarity.Formats in code (docs/FORMATS-PLAN.md, "XML"): `read list<Order> from xml text at "shop/orders/order"` and `xml of orders at "shop/orders/order"`. `at` is a path of local names with slashes (a leading slash allowed): the first is the root element's name, the middle ones are descended into (the first of that name), the last names the record's elements; a list is every element of that name there, possibly none, one record the first (none is an error that names the path, as a missing step names the path walked so far). Without `at` a list is the root element's child elements and one record the root element. Bytes become text by a byte order mark (UTF-8, UTF-16), else the declaration's encoding (utf-8, windows-1252, iso-8859-1), else UTF-8. Names match by local name (a prefix ignored); fields as JSON's names do, ignoring case, underscores, hyphens and spaces, the exact name first. A field takes the text of a child element of its name, else an attribute of its name (namespace declarations are none); an empty one is left out, so the record keeps its default. A record field takes the element of its name. A list field takes the elements of its name; when there is one of them and its child elements all have one name that is not a field of the item's entity, those children are the items; one empty element is an empty list. No other name is guessed. `other` fields are never read. Values are then fitted as JSON's are, with "XML" in the messages. Writing always takes `at`: the elements around the records and the record's own (a list needs both). The XML declaration first (`encoding`: UTF-8, windows-1252 or ISO-8859-1; a character the encoding cannot hold as a character reference), each field in the entity's order as a child element of its name, null, the id and `other` fields left out, a list of values as repeated elements of the field's name, a list of records inside an element of the field's name with one element per record named after its entity in camelCase, a record field as an element of its name holding its fields; values in Clarity's one form; `indent true` one element a line; `namespace` as `xmlns` on the outermost element. `read` cases give `fitted` or `error`, `write` cases `written` or `error`, word for word; `roundTrip` cases are written with `options` and read back with their `at`, giving `value` again.

read.name: the design's example: attributes and child elements, a record field, a list inside one element whose children have one name, a prefix ignored, other kinds left out
read.input:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!-- export -->
<shop xmlns:o="urn:o">
  <orders>
    <o:order number="A-1" placed="2026-11-01" owner="7">
      <customer><name>Ada</name></customer>
      <lines><line product="Coffee" quantity="2"/><line product="Tea" quantity="1"/></lines>
      <note>leave at door</note>
    </o:order>
    <order number="A-2" total="12.50" paid="true" status="closed"/>
  </orders>
</shop>

read.name: a child element comes before an attribute of the same name
names match ignoring case, underscores, hyphens and spaces, the exact name first; the path matches local names exactly
an empty element or attribute is left out, so the record keeps its default; space between elements is no text
text keeps its spaces, entities, character references and CDATA; comments are left aside
a list of values: the elements of its name, repeated
a list of values: one element of its name holding elements of one name
a list of values: one element of its name with only text is one item, an empty one an empty list
a list of records: the elements of its name, repeated
a list of records: one element of its name with attributes is one item, an empty one an empty list
a list of records: one element whose children all have the name of a field of the item is one item, not a wrapper
no other name is guessed: <line> elements directly inside the record do not fill lines
without at a list is the root element's child elements, whatever their names
without at one record is the root element
one record at a path is the first element of the last name
a list at a path with no elements of the last name is empty
a leading slash in the path is allowed
a list at a path of one name is the root element when it has that name
a value at the top: the element's text
a list of values at the top: the texts of the elements of the last name
a missing step says the path walked so far
a root element of another name
one record at a path that holds none
a value that does not fit says where, as JSON's do

write.name: a list of records inside the elements of the path: fields in the entity's order as child elements, null and other kinds and the id left out, a list of values repeated, a list of records inside an element of its name with one element per record named after its entity in camelCase
indent true writes one element a line; namespace the default namespace on the outermost element
one record: at names the elements around it and its own
one record at one name is the root element
an empty list writes the elements around it
a value: the last element holds its text
a list of values: one element per item named by the last step
a character the encoding cannot hold is a character reference
without at nothing is written

write.name: a list needs an element around its items
write.error: xml of a list needs the element around its items and the item's own: at "orders/order"
